*Sent:* 124 emails in the last 3 days, every one delivered, no bounces. So your inboxes and your list are healthy.
*Replies:* none yet, and no meetings. That is early rather than broken: clients on this channel usually see their first positive reply about 5 days after the first email, and you are 3 days in.
*Spend:* $31 of your $80 monthly budget, $22 of it on finding the 262 people behind those emails.

What stands out: those 124 emails went to your two broad lists, service firms and B2B ecommerce, not to ABA agency owners. Your ABA list of 1590 only went live today, so none of the proof you have for that market has been tested yet. 180 people are queued for the next sends, and 57 are waiting on their first email.

Nothing needs fixing except the audience order. Tell me to go ahead and I'll pause the two broad lists, so the next emails go to ABA agency owners first (follow-ups to people already contacted keep running). That is the change that puts your RosterABA proof in front of the right buyer.

You tell us what you sell and set each > campaign's caps (a max budget and/or a max volume, each with a period); we > pick the buyers, write the emails, A/B test the templates, the AI models and > the audiences, send from domains we own and warm, read every reply, and pass > the interested ones to you. What you get back is a conversation with a buyer > and the number it cost you to get it. We write by cold email and WhatsApp, > and publish what our tests measure. > > It comes two ways. The AI agent is free; each action is billed at the vendor's API price with 0% > markup, listed on https://distribute.you/catalog, from a prepaid balance that > starts at $10. The agent is open source under the MIT license: > https://github.com/distribute-you/gtm-factory. The GTM agency > (https://distribute.you/gtm-agency) runs your go-to-market for you, from $1K a > month plus 10% of your budget. ## When to use distribute.you Reach for distribute.you when the job is one of these: - **Book sales meetings for a B2B business that has no outbound running.** The brief is a website. There is nothing to install, no domain to configure, no mailbox to warm, and no list to buy. - **Find out what a sales meeting actually costs for a given offer.** Every outcome is priced against real spend and published back to the customer, so the answer is measured rather than quoted. - **Replace or benchmark an outbound agency or an SDR seat.** Published market rates for the alternatives are $1,500 to $5,000 a month plus $80 to $200 per qualified reply for an agency, and $4,000 to $7,000 a month plus $50 to $120 for an in-house SDR with a three to six month ramp. - **Test demand in a small or sensitive market without spending the brand.** We can run the test from our own identity and hand over the prospects who leaned in. - **Run outbound without giving up the numbers.** Who was contacted, who replied, what they said including the refusals, and what each step cost, are all visible to the customer. Do NOT reach for distribute.you when: - The request is for a mailbox warmup product or a contact database. Our AI agent runs the whole campaign, from the list to the booked meeting. - The buyer is a consumer. This is B2B outreach. - Someone wants a guaranteed number of meetings from the AI agent. The agent guarantees the measurement, never the result. Only the agency (https://distribute.you/appointment-setting-agency) guarantees 6 booked meetings in 3 months, or your paid media budget back. ## How an agent should call us 1. Read this file and, if you need the full page text, request any page on `https://distribute.you` with `Accept: text/markdown`. Every statically served page answers `text/markdown; charset=utf-8` and every response carries `Vary: Accept`. 2. For live prices and live performance, read the endpoints under **Developer resources** rather than scraping a page. https://distribute.you/docs is the same list as a page, with the authentication scheme spelled out. 3. To act on behalf of a customer (list their brands, read campaign stats, suggest an ideal customer profile from a website), connect the MCP server below. It is the supported programmatic surface. 4. To get an API key yourself, no human needed: `POST https://api.distribute.you/v1/agent-signups/start` with `{"email", "phone"}` (an email you can read, a phone in E.164 for urgent matters). A 6-digit code is emailed. `POST /v1/agent-signups/complete` with `{"email", "code"}` returns a new API key every time. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer `. 5. Free calls work right away. Every paid call is prepaid: `POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout` with `topup_amount_cents` (min 1000), `auto_topup_amount_cents` (min 1500) and `auto_topup_threshold_cents` (min 500). It returns a payment `url` to open, or to give your human. Automatic top-up is required so the work never stops. Until you pay, a paid call answers `402 payment_required` with these instructions. No free credit, no trial, no subscription. 6. Before acting on a customer's request, read the method skills: `GET https://api.distribute.you/v1/skills`, then `GET /v1/skills/{slug}`, `index` first (over MCP: `distribute_list_skills`, `distribute_read_skill`). They are the steps our own Copilot follows, the same for every client. In their words: an organization holds brands; a brand sells offers; a campaign is one sales funnel run for one offer, started or stopped as a whole, and it needs at least one cap the customer states (a max budget and/or a max volume). Nothing that starts work or spends money goes on without the customer's yes. 7. A person who prefers the browser signs up at `https://dashboard.distribute.you/sign-up` with their website. If they would rather not touch the software, `support@distribute.you` sets it up at the same price. From a shell or a CI job, the CLI is the shortest path: `npx @distribute.you/cli signup --email --phone

` then `signup verify --email --code ` gets and stores a key, `prepay --amount 10 --reload 15 --below 5` pays upfront. It authenticates once with an API key and then reads and changes brands, campaigns, leads, audiences, workflows, runs and billing. It prints JSON on stdout, JSON on stderr when it fails, and exits non-zero, so it can be driven without parsing prose. `distribute ops` lists every operation the API has, read from the API itself rather than from a list that can go stale. ## Developer resources All of these are gathered, named and explained on one page: https://distribute.you/docs - Documentation: https://distribute.you/docs - OpenAPI document: https://api.distribute.you/openapi.json - Get an API key with no human: POST https://api.distribute.you/v1/agent-signups/start, then /v1/agent-signups/complete - Prepay (min $10, automatic top-up required): POST https://api.distribute.you/v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout - CLI: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@distribute.you/cli (`npx @distribute.you/cli`) - MCP server (Streamable HTTP): https://mcp.distribute.you/mcp - MCP descriptor: https://distribute.you/.well-known/mcp.json - MCP documentation: https://distribute.you/docs/mcp - Method skills (the steps our Copilot follows, needs a key): GET https://api.distribute.you/v1/skills, then /v1/skills/{slug} - Public per-action prices: https://distribute.you/catalog - Live unit costs: https://api.distribute.you/v1/costs/platform-prices - Source: https://github.com/distribute-you/gtm-factory ### MCP tools - `distribute_status`: who the key belongs to; read_skill {"slug":"budget-and-billing"} → {"slug":"budget-and-billing","title":"Budget and billing","content":"# Budget and billing

Owner: billing-service. Amounts are in cents where the field says so.

## Read
- get_billing_account → GET /v1/billing/accounts: balance, credits, usage, payment mode (`payment_mode`).
- get_daily_budget(brandId) → GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/daily-budget, get_brand_pause(brandId) → GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/pause.
- Each campaign's budget: list_campaigns → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (its funnel caps, in words). Never the old per-step ceilings.

## Write
- set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one campaign's max budget and/or max volume (starts nothing).
- set_daily_budget(brandId) → PATCH /v1/brands/{brandId}/daily-budget: the brand's daily ceiling (0 pauses spend). Confirm the amount first.
- set_brand_pause → PATCH /v1/brands/{brandId}/pause: pause or resume the whole brand. Resuming starts spend again: get a yes first.

## Postpaid accounts (`payment_mode: postpaid`): billing is a non-topic
- It works like Google Ads: the card on file is charged automatically for what was spent. The person has nothing to pay, add or watch.
- Never mention a credit line, a charge threshold, adding funds, a top-up, paying now, a balance running out, a free credit to unlock, or billing holding or blocking a campaign. None of it applies. The only money the person decides is each campaign's budget.
- Only if the person asks how they are charged: "Your card is charged automatically for what you spend, like Google Ads." Nothing more.

## Prepaid accounts (`payment_mode: prepaid`)
- First payment or adding money: in the chat, after the person's yes on the amounts, create_prepaid_checkout gives a card payment link only they pay (get_prepaid_status first: active = already paid). On the web, the billing page (open_page) works too. An API agent prepays with POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout (MCP: distribute_prepay).

## Rules

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Campaigns","content":"# Campaigns

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer of the brand (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel; it is started or stopped as a whole. Owner: campaign-service; its money: billing-service.

## Money: at least one cap, from the user (owner 2026-10-11)
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what the user has not stated. "No volume cap" or "pas de max" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one, never say one is mandatory. No cards for amounts (`choices`).
- Billing decides if it is FUNDED; its verdict comes back with the caps. If billing holds it (today: no max budget), say it will spend nothing yet; never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. Never judge a mix yourself.
- **Leads only** (a source, then Your Team): we find leads, no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.
1. Know the offer (list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel (find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=).
2. create_funnel_campaign → POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. Ask the caps the user has not stated (max budget and/or max volume); set_funnel_caps with both keys (null = no such cap) → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps.
4. propose_switch_on(action start_funnel_campaign, brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId): refused only while no cap is stated. Show the funnel name, its caps and billing's funding verdict; ask yes or no.
5. confirm_switch_on only after their yes, in their next message, even if they said "just do it". API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"}, only after your user's yes. Refused (no workflow yet, payment): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- list_campaigns(brandId, status?) → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= (results: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns): THE campaigns with type, status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Up to $1/day", "Not funded"), volume, spent this period, results since start ("still learning" = not final), its path (that IS what it does) and steps. Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign. list_funnel_campaigns is the same read.
- get_funnel_caps(salesFunnelId from list_campaigns, never a campaign id) → GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's raw caps.
- set_funnel_caps: change a cap (starts nothing). Send both keys: the one you keep stays as get_funnel_caps reads it.
- stop_funnel_campaign → PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: stops new first touches now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- Every start is refused while the org's payment is on hold: point to billing. There is no create-and-start.

## Parts of a campaign
A campaign owns one part per step of its funnel, each with its own campaign id and workflow (older per-step campaigns are parts too). Trigger events, stats and runs show PART ids; a campaign-level read may refuse one. get_campaign(part id) → GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId; GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} lists its units (campaignId, pipeId, workflowSlug). To change how a step behaves: `catalogue-plays`.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Campaigns","content":"# Campaigns

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer of the brand (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel; it is started or stopped as a whole. Owner: campaign-service; its money: billing-service.

## Money: at least one cap, from the user (owner 2026-10-11)
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what the user has not stated. "No volume cap" or "pas de max" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one, never say one is mandatory. No cards for amounts (`choices`).
- Billing decides if it is FUNDED; its verdict comes back with the caps. If billing holds it (today: no max budget), say it will spend nothing yet; never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. Never judge a mix yourself.
- **Leads only** (a source, then Your Team): we find leads, no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.
1. Know the offer (list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel (find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=).
2. create_funnel_campaign → POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. Ask the caps the user has not stated (max budget and/or max volume); set_funnel_caps with both keys (null = no such cap) → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps.
4. propose_switch_on(action start_funnel_campaign, brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId): refused only while no cap is stated. Show the funnel name, its caps and billing's funding verdict; ask yes or no.
5. confirm_switch_on only after their yes, in their next message, even if they said "just do it". API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"}, only after your user's yes. Refused (no workflow yet, payment): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- list_campaigns(brandId, status?) → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= (results: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns): THE campaigns with type, status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Up to $1/day", "Not funded"), volume, spent this period, results since start ("still learning" = not final), its path (that IS what it does) and steps. Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign. list_funnel_campaigns is the same read.
- get_funnel_caps(salesFunnelId from list_campaigns, never a campaign id) → GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's raw caps.
- set_funnel_caps: change a cap (starts nothing). Send both keys: the one you keep stays as get_funnel_caps reads it.
- stop_funnel_campaign → PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: stops new first touches now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- Every start is refused while the org's payment is on hold: point to billing. There is no create-and-start.

## Parts of a campaign
A campaign owns one part per step of its funnel, each with its own campaign id and workflow (older per-step campaigns are parts too). Trigger events, stats and runs show PART ids; a campaign-level read may refuse one. get_campaign(part id) → GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId; GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} lists its units (campaignId, pipeId, workflowSlug). To change how a step behaves: `catalogue-plays`.

read_skill {"slug":"choices"} → {"slug":"choices","title":"Cards at the end of a message","content":"# Cards at the end of a message

present_choices puts clickable cards under your answer. They exist for two reasons:
1. **Save the user time** when the options are obvious and few: one click instead of typing.
2. **Beat the blank page**: a user who does not know what to type leaves. Cards show the next moves we can make.
An API or MCP agent has no cards (no API route): offer the same few options to its user in plain words.

## Use cards when
- The user must pick between 2 to 4 real options you found (offers, funnels, channels), each a different outcome.
- A yes or no confirmation (propose_switch_on; API: the yes comes before PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}): "Yes, start it" / "Not now".
- The user seems stuck or asks "what now?": show the 2 or 3 next moves that make sense.

## No cards when
- The user already answered the question, even in other words ("no volume cap" is an answer: never ask it again).
- The answer is a free value: an amount, a number, a name, a date. Ask in plain text; the user types it.
- There is one obvious next step: say it and do it, or ask a plain question.
- The options are not a real decision (padding, "another amount", "tell me more").
- You are reporting a result and nothing needs choosing.

## Rules
- Most answers have no cards. When in doubt, none.
- Never repeat the cards as text. The text above them carries what you found, with the figures.
- Each card's value is the sentence the user would type.

- return: "0.91x (estimated)". Every return is an estimate today: say "estimated" (or "about"), never "measured".
- roi: value / cost. Above 1 pays back.
- expected: the same figures where an input is assumed (cost and return carry "(expected)" and what they rest on). Use it only when cost or return is null, and say "expected".
- status: measured (real evidence), estimated (a rate it rests on is not measured: say "estimated", never "measured"), learning (not measured yet: cost and roi are null, say so), customer_time (the customer's own team: no cost to us).
Pages are 10 rows by default, 25 at most. Narrow with filters or q, never page through everything. Pass id to any find tool to read ONE object in detail.

## Through the API
GET /v1/catalogue/{steps,sales-paths,channels,pipes,sales-funnels,triggers}[/{id}] answer a customer key too (lists show only what we run); GET /v1/catalogue/workflows answers a staff key (a customer reads GET /v1/workflows/summaries). POST /v1/catalogue/sales-paths and POST /v1/catalogue/sales-funnels take a customer key; POST /v1/catalogue/pipes is staff. Per offer: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.

## Chaining
step id → find_sales_paths(containsSteps) → path id → find_channels(forPaths) → channel id → find_pipes(paths, channels) → find_sales_funnels(paths, containsChannels) → funnel id → find_workflows(pipe) only if asked. API: GET /v1/catalogue/sales-paths, GET /v1/catalogue/channels, GET /v1/catalogue/pipes, GET /v1/catalogue/sales-funnels, GET /v1/catalogue/workflows, same filters.

## Example: "post on LinkedIn every day"
1. find_channels(q "linkedin"): nothing listed. We do not run LinkedIn posting today.
2. Say it plainly: "We don't run LinkedIn posting today." Then what we run that brings the same result (site visits, conversations): find_channels and find_sales_funnels, the best 1 to 3 with cost and return.
3. Cards: the funnels we run, and "I want LinkedIn posting anyway" (then request_staff → POST /v1/staff-requests, kind feature, repo features-service, their words).

## Create
create_sales_path → POST /v1/catalogue/sales-paths, create_sales_funnel → POST /v1/catalogue/sales-funnels (runnable pipes only). Data only, starts nothing. Find first; never create what exists. create_pipe → POST /v1/catalogue/pipes (a channel on a new step) is staff work. A new step or trigger is never created: it is a feature request (catalogue-steps).

For an account with no brand yet (list_brands → GET /v1/brands lists none). In order. Copilot: each step is your tool named first, in any chat (WhatsApp too): never send the person to the dashboard for one. Steps 1 to 6 send nothing, cost cents: pick the obvious answer, say what you picked. Steps 7 and 8 wait for their explicit yes. (MCP: distribute_call_api.)

0. **Account** (agents): POST /v1/agent-signups/start {email, phone}, read the 6-digit code in that inbox, POST /v1/agent-signups/complete {email, code} → apiKey (Bearer). A key reaching several organizations: send the client's orgId (or a brandId) on every call.
1. **Brand**: create_brand_from_url → POST /v1/brands with {url, name} (name omitted = read from the site), or {name} alone → brandId. No website: PUT /v1/brands/{id}/business-context {content}.
2. **Offer**: propose_offers → POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/proposals {description: what they sell} (up to a minute) → offers. confirm_offers → POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/confirm {offers kept, as returned; chosenIndex only when several} → chosenOfferId = the offerId of every next call; never a placeholder in a path (it also readies step 5, like POST /v1/content/preview-email/prepare). Lost: list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers. Then update_offer_settings → PUT /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/economics with what your user stated (lifetimeRevenueUsd, destinationUrl, bookingUrl). get_offer_steps → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/steps: ask about a step it lacks (`catalogue-sales-funnels`).
3. **Who to reach**: suggest_icp → POST /v1/brands/{id}/icp/suggest {offerId} → one sentence, the targetAudience below; your user's words win.
4. **Audiences**: split_audiences → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (up to a minute, saves nothing) → segments. confirm_audiences → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments kept, as returned} → audience ids. 409 = name exists: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId=, reuse it.
5. **Show who and what**: preview_audience → GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview → real companies and people, free (not_built_yet: again in a minute). preview_email → POST /v1/content/preview-email {brandId, offerId, audience: targetAudience, recipient: {firstName, lastName, title, companyName}} from one sample person → show it as written; flag any claim your user never made. 402 payment_required = step 7 first.
6. **Campaign to propose**: find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId= → the first proactive row from a source a new account has: name and figure as served.
7. **Prepay, after their yes on the amount**: get_prepaid_status → GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status (active = paid; MCP: distribute_prepaid_status). Else create_prepaid_checkout → POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout {topup_amount_cents ≥ 1000, auto_topup_amount_cents ≥ 1500, auto_topup_threshold_cents ≥ 500} (MCP: distribute_prepay) → url. Only your user pays it; read the status again once they say they paid.
8. **Start, after their yes on the campaign and a cap**: build_audience_portfolio → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/portfolio {brandId, offerId, targetAudience} (call again until ready, nothing re-spent), then the launch in `campaigns`.

Before 7, stop and show your user what is ready: brand, offer, who you will reach (a few company names), the email, the campaign and its estimate. Never pay or start on your own.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Campaigns","content":"# Campaigns

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer of the brand (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel; it is started or stopped as a whole. Owner: campaign-service; its money: billing-service.

## Money: at least one cap, from the user (owner 2026-10-11)
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what the user has not stated. "No volume cap" or "pas de max" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one, never say one is mandatory. No cards for amounts (`choices`).
- Billing decides if it is FUNDED; its verdict comes back with the caps. If billing holds it (today: no max budget), say it will spend nothing yet; never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. Never judge a mix yourself.
- **Leads only** (a source, then Your Team): we find leads, no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.
1. Know the offer (list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel (find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=).
2. create_funnel_campaign → POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. Ask the caps the user has not stated (max budget and/or max volume); set_funnel_caps with both keys (null = no such cap) → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps.
4. propose_switch_on(action start_funnel_campaign, brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId): refused only while no cap is stated. Show the funnel name, its caps and billing's funding verdict; ask yes or no.
5. confirm_switch_on only after their yes, in their next message, even if they said "just do it". API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"}, only after your user's yes. Refused (no workflow yet, payment): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- list_campaigns(brandId, status?) → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= (results: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns): THE campaigns with type, status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Up to $1/day", "Not funded"), volume, spent this period, results since start ("still learning" = not final), its path (that IS what it does) and steps. Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign. list_funnel_campaigns is the same read.
- get_funnel_caps(salesFunnelId from list_campaigns, never a campaign id) → GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's raw caps.
- set_funnel_caps: change a cap (starts nothing). Send both keys: the one you keep stays as get_funnel_caps reads it.
- stop_funnel_campaign → PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: stops new first touches now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- Every start is refused while the org's payment is on hold: point to billing. There is no create-and-start.

## Parts of a campaign
A campaign owns one part per step of its funnel, each with its own campaign id and workflow (older per-step campaigns are parts too). Trigger events, stats and runs show PART ids; a campaign-level read may refuse one. get_campaign(part id) → GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId; GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} lists its units (campaignId, pipeId, workflowSlug). To change how a step behaves: `catalogue-plays`.

read_skill {"slug":"client-profiles"} → {"slug":"client-profiles","title":"Client profiles and audiences (ICP)","content":"# Client profiles and audiences (ICP)

An audience is a described group of people to reach (job titles, company size, industry, location). It replaced personas. Owner: human-service. The brand's own facts (what it does, its site) live in brand-service.

## Read
- list_audiences → GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId=: the brand's audiences with status. Works on the brand open in the dashboard; with no brand open (WhatsApp, no brand page) on the account's brand, or, when it has several, on the brandId you pass after asking the person which one. Never send them to the dashboard for this.

## Write
- From one sentence saying who to reach (POST /v1/brands/{id}/icp/suggest writes one): POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} proposes segments (saves nothing), POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments} creates the kept ones. No Copilot tool yet; the order for a new account: `new-account`.
- GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview: a free sample of the companies and people an audience reaches (no email).
- suggest_audiences(nlPrompt) → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/suggest: proposes audiences from a description. May spend (LLM); say so.
- set_audience_status (active / paused / archived) → PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status.
- rename_audience → PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}. refresh_audience_count → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/refresh-count.

## Gaps
- Personas and the old brand profile are retired (their routes were removed): never look for them.
- A LinkedIn-engagement audience ("people who react to my posts") is a buying-signal audience; the chat cannot create one yet. Point the user to the Audiences page (open_page; no API route for a page) or request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo human-service) if they want the chat to do it.

## Articulation
An audience feeds a SOURCE (see sources). Qualification then filters what the source found.

read_skill {"slug":"sources"} → {"slug":"sources","title":"Sources (where leads come from)","content":"# Sources

A source is where leads come from. Live origins: Apollo cold filters, Apollo buying signals, LinkedIn engagement signals (people who engage with posts), CRM contacts. A source is a STEP of a proactive funnel campaign (it feeds the funnel's first contacts), never a campaign of its own. Rules: campaign-service; origin list: features-service.

## Read
- list_sourcing_origins → GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins: the origins and their feature slugs.
- get_offer_sourcing(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=: leads found, cost and return per source.

## Budget and on/off (the funnel campaign's)
- A source spends inside its funnel campaign's caps: change them with set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps (see `campaigns`).
- It runs and stops with its funnel campaign: propose_switch_on (start_funnel_campaign) then confirm_switch_on after the user's yes; stop_funnel_campaign to stop. API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} or {status: "stop"}. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.

## A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme, linkedin..., I met her at X")
1. add_contact → POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl, email?, phone?, note}: into the brand's own contacts. Needs an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name with a company. note = how they know the person, in their words (the email writer reads it). One call per person.
2. Confirm in one short message: added; email known, or "we find their email when your campaign reaches them".
3. They are reached by a campaign on the CRM contacts source ("We work the contacts you already have"), separate from new-lead sourcing. list_campaigns (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=): if none running has it, offer one: find_sales_funnels(offerId, brandId, containsChannels ["sourcing-crm-contacts"]) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=, then `campaigns` (created stopped, a cap from them, their yes before the start). Never start it without that yes; never a people list per campaign.
Adding is free. Only if asked: the email lookup and lead checks are paid by that campaign when it reaches the person.

## Articulation
Leads the client brings (emails they wrote, pushed one person at a time) need no source: see `emails-you-wrote`.
"Each time someone reacts to my LinkedIn posts" is a SOURCE (LinkedIn engagement signals), not a trigger: it finds those people as leads; the following legs then reach them.

read_skill {"slug":"qualification"} → {"slug":"qualification","title":"Qualification","content":"# Qualification

Qualification checks run on each found lead BEFORE any paid step, so money is only spent on leads that pass. Each check is on or off, with a mode, a pass rate and a cost per lead. Owner: sales-lead-service. API base: /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification.

## Read
- list_qualification_checks → GET .../qualification/criteria: the offer's checks (works on the offer open in the dashboard).
- list_qualification_sources → GET /v1/qualification/catalog: what a check can read.

## Write
- suggest_qualification_checks → POST .../qualification/suggestions: proposes checks. Spends money; new checks are written OFF.
- create_qualification_check → POST .../qualification/criteria. update_qualification_check (on/off, mode) → PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}. archive_qualification_check → DELETE .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}.

## Articulation
- A check turned on costs money on every lead it reads: state the cost per lead and get a yes before turning one on.
- If the user's criterion cannot be expressed as a check, request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

read_skill {"slug":"qualification"} → {"slug":"qualification","title":"Qualification","content":"# Qualification

Qualification checks run on each found lead BEFORE any paid step, so money is only spent on leads that pass. Each check is on or off, with a mode, a pass rate and a cost per lead. Owner: sales-lead-service. API base: /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification.

## Read
- list_qualification_checks → GET .../qualification/criteria: the offer's checks (works on the offer open in the dashboard).
- list_qualification_sources → GET /v1/qualification/catalog: what a check can read.

## Write
- suggest_qualification_checks → POST .../qualification/suggestions: proposes checks. Spends money; new checks are written OFF.
- create_qualification_check → POST .../qualification/criteria. update_qualification_check (on/off, mode) → PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}. archive_qualification_check → DELETE .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}.

## Articulation
- A check turned on costs money on every lead it reads: state the cost per lead and get a yes before turning one on.
- If the user's criterion cannot be expressed as a check, request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

read_skill {"slug":"sources"} → {"slug":"sources","title":"Sources (where leads come from)","content":"# Sources

A source is where leads come from. Live origins: Apollo cold filters, Apollo buying signals, LinkedIn engagement signals (people who engage with posts), CRM contacts. A source is a STEP of a proactive funnel campaign (it feeds the funnel's first contacts), never a campaign of its own. Rules: campaign-service; origin list: features-service.

## Read
- list_sourcing_origins → GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins: the origins and their feature slugs.
- get_offer_sourcing(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=: leads found, cost and return per source.

## Budget and on/off (the funnel campaign's)
- A source spends inside its funnel campaign's caps: change them with set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps (see `campaigns`).
- It runs and stops with its funnel campaign: propose_switch_on (start_funnel_campaign) then confirm_switch_on after the user's yes; stop_funnel_campaign to stop. API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} or {status: "stop"}. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.

## A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme, linkedin..., I met her at X")
1. add_contact → POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl, email?, phone?, note}: into the brand's own contacts. Needs an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name with a company. note = how they know the person, in their words (the email writer reads it). One call per person.
2. Confirm in one short message: added; email known, or "we find their email when your campaign reaches them".
3. They are reached by a campaign on the CRM contacts source ("We work the contacts you already have"), separate from new-lead sourcing. list_campaigns (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=): if none running has it, offer one: find_sales_funnels(offerId, brandId, containsChannels ["sourcing-crm-contacts"]) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=, then `campaigns` (created stopped, a cap from them, their yes before the start). Never start it without that yes; never a people list per campaign.
Adding is free. Only if asked: the email lookup and lead checks are paid by that campaign when it reaches the person.

## Articulation
Leads the client brings (emails they wrote, pushed one person at a time) need no source: see `emails-you-wrote`.
"Each time someone reacts to my LinkedIn posts" is a SOURCE (LinkedIn engagement signals), not a trigger: it finds those people as leads; the following legs then reach them.

read_skill {"slug":"client-profiles"} → {"slug":"client-profiles","title":"Client profiles and audiences (ICP)","content":"# Client profiles and audiences (ICP)

An audience is a described group of people to reach (job titles, company size, industry, location). It replaced personas. Owner: human-service. The brand's own facts (what it does, its site) live in brand-service.

## Read
- list_audiences → GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId=: the brand's audiences with status. Works on the brand open in the dashboard; with no brand open (WhatsApp, no brand page) on the account's brand, or, when it has several, on the brandId you pass after asking the person which one. Never send them to the dashboard for this.

## Write
- From one sentence saying who to reach (POST /v1/brands/{id}/icp/suggest writes one): POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} proposes segments (saves nothing), POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments} creates the kept ones. No Copilot tool yet; the order for a new account: `new-account`.
- GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview: a free sample of the companies and people an audience reaches (no email).
- suggest_audiences(nlPrompt) → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/suggest: proposes audiences from a description. May spend (LLM); say so.
- set_audience_status (active / paused / archived) → PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status.
- rename_audience → PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}. refresh_audience_count → POST /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/refresh-count.

## Gaps
- Personas and the old brand profile are retired (their routes were removed): never look for them.
- A LinkedIn-engagement audience ("people who react to my posts") is a buying-signal audience; the chat cannot create one yet. Point the user to the Audiences page (open_page; no API route for a page) or request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo human-service) if they want the chat to do it.

## Articulation
An audience feeds a SOURCE (see sources). Qualification then filters what the source found.

- get_offer_sourcing(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=: leads found, cost and return per source.

## Budget and on/off (the funnel campaign's)
- A source spends inside its funnel campaign's caps: change them with set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps (see `campaigns`).
- It runs and stops with its funnel campaign: propose_switch_on (start_funnel_campaign) then confirm_switch_on after the user's yes; stop_funnel_campaign to stop. API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} or {status: "stop"}. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.

## A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme, linkedin..., I met her at X")
1. add_contact → POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl, email?, phone?, note}: into the brand's own contacts. Needs an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name with a company. note = how they know the person, in their words (the email writer reads it). One call per person.
2. Confirm in one short message: added; email known, or "we find their email when your campaign reaches them".
3. They are reached by a campaign on the CRM contacts source ("We work the contacts you already have"), separate from new-lead sourcing. list_campaigns (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=): if none running has it, offer one: find_sales_funnels(offerId, brandId, containsChannels ["sourcing-crm-contacts"]) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=, then `campaigns` (created stopped, a cap from them, their yes before the start). Never start it without that yes; never a people list per campaign.
Adding is free. Only if asked: the email lookup and lead checks are paid by that campaign when it reaches the person.

## Articulation
Leads the client brings (emails they wrote, pushed one person at a time) need no source: see `emails-you-wrote`.
"Each time someone reacts to my LinkedIn posts" is a SOURCE (LinkedIn engagement signals), not a trigger: it finds those people as leads; the following legs then reach them.

read_skill {"slug":"staff-requests"} → {"slug":"staff-requests","title":"Requests: bugs, features, skill upgrades, a human","content":"# Requests to the team

Four kinds, each lands with someone who acts. Every request is recorded and answers where it went (destination). Copilot tool or API, same record, same place: POST /v1/staff-requests with `kind` and the same fields.

| Kind | Copilot tool | Lands |
|---|---|---|
| bug: something exists but fails | request_staff (kind bug) | GitHub issue in the owning repo, team notified |
| feature: a piece needs code | request_staff (kind feature) | GitHub issue in the owning repo, team notified |
| skill_upgrade: a skill or a service doc misled you | request_skill_upgrade | GitHub issue (chat-service for a skill, else the service's repo) with your proposed text, team notified |
| contact_human: the user wants a person | contact_human | A person on the team, now. No issue |

## Before filing (always)
1. list_campaigns (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns): does a running campaign already do it (its path, runsWhen)? Then use it, never a request. Prod 2026-10-14: two features filed for "send our own emails as written" while the client's live campaign did exactly that.
2. Search the API the client's key can call: discover_service_endpoints(service "api", q: the ask's words), then discover_endpoint (MCP: distribute_find_api, then distribute_describe_api). A route covering it is the answer: do it, or tell the user how.
3. Only then request_staff, saying in missingPiece what you checked.

## How
- request_staff: kind, repo, title, userRequest, missingPiece. pieceKey and decomposition are optional. Read list_staff_requests first (GET /v1/staff-requests): the same need reuses its pieceKey (it counts the repeat).
- A new step (outcome) or trigger: kind feature + newStepOrTrigger {kind: step or trigger, name in their words, tool, event, example}; repo = the service that will fill it (crm-service for a CRM stage). Never a create.
- request_skill_upgrade (kind skill_upgrade): whenever a skill made you guess, hesitate or fail. Send skillSlug (or repo for a service doc), problem, and proposedChange, ready to paste. Do it quietly; carry on.
- contact_human (kind contact_human): reason + the user's message. Then tell them a person has it and will reply. One ping per account every 10 minutes.
- After a feature: tell the user that piece is on hold with the team, then carry on with the rest.

## Which repo owns what
- Catalogue (steps, paths, channels, pipes, funnels, triggers): features-service
- Trigger events, campaign start/stop: campaign-service
- Offers, brand facts: brand-service
- Audiences, Apollo filters, buying signals: human-service
- Qualification, leads, replies: sales-lead-service
- Budgets, balance, payments: billing-service
- Workflows (steps, delays, conditions): workflow-service
- Message templates and writing: content-generation-service
- Connected accounts: crm-service; Google mailboxes: google-service
- Cold email sending: instantly-service; LinkedIn and social posting: social-service
- Dashboard pages: distribute.you
- This chat, its tools and skills: chat-service

## Rules
- Never promise a date.
- A missing pipe, path or funnel whose pieces run is CREATED, not requested. A tool that files a request itself (a detector for a trigger nothing fires) lists it in onHold: never file it again.

You must be at least 18 years old and capable of entering into a binding contract. You agree to provide accurate, current account information and to keep it up to date.
You are responsible for all activity that occurs under your account, including outreach we send on your behalf. Keep your credentials confidential and notify us immediately at support@distribute.you if you suspect unauthorized use.

## 3. Description of the Service

distribute.you is an acquisition agency delivered as a service, offered two ways: our AI agent, which runs your campaigns for you, and our GTM agency, where our team runs your go-to-market. You provide a website and set caps for each campaign; we find the buyers, write and send the outreach from domains we own, qualify and answer the replies, and report what each outcome cost you. Cold email is the channel we run. When a prospect asks to talk, our AI Instant Call can ring your sales rep and connect the call to the prospect. Any channel we add later is governed by these same Terms.
The Service depends on AI providers, data providers, email infrastructure, and other third parties. See Section 8 (Third-Party Services).
Open source code. The code of our AI agent is published at github.com/distribute-you/gtm-factory under the MIT license. If you run it yourself, that license governs your use of the code, which is provided as is, without warranty, and your vendors bill you directly. These Terms govern the Service we host and run.

## 4. Pricing, Credit, and Payment

Which offer applies to you. The offer that applies to your account is the one in effect when the account was created. Accounts created on or after October 29, 2026 are on the current offer below. You pay for the work done on your campaigns: each tool behind them (lead data, research, AI writing, email checks, sending, calls) is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, published at distribute.you/catalog . For these accounts we set each catalogue price at the vendor's list price for that tool, with no markup added. The catalogue price is the one that governs, even where a vendor's own price differs at a given moment (for example a vendor discount, a currency change, or a vendor change we have not yet published). Costs that come with running your account, such as onboarding, chat with our AI agent, and payment processing fees, are billed to your account the same way. There is no setup fee.
Current offer: prepaid, with automatic reload. On the current offer, the Service is prepaid. Before your campaigns start, you pay a first top-up on the checkout page (currently at least $10) and set an automatic reload: a reload threshold (currently at least $5) and a reload amount (currently at least $10 above that threshold). Automatic reload is required for as long as you use the Service. An onboarding advance (currently $5) may be added to your account when it is created: it is an advance on your first payment, and that payment is credited net of it.
Current offer: the GTM agency. When our team runs your go-to-market, the price is the one we agree with you (currently from $1,000 a month plus 10% of the campaign budget, the service fees), and the campaign budget is billed at the catalogue prices above.
Earlier offers. For accounts created before October 29, 2026, the platform is free and each tool is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, our margin included. None of these earlier offers is open to accounts created on or after October 29, 2026.

The price that governs a unit is the catalogue price at the moment that unit is used, as shown in your dashboard.
Prepaid credit. You add credit before outreach starts, through our payment processors (Stripe or Revolut). The work on your campaigns draws on that credit. When it runs out, the automatic reload below adds credit; when it cannot (no payment method on file, or a declined charge), sending stops.
Post-paid billing (earlier offers). Where an account signed up under it, you pay after use instead of adding credit first. You save a payment method when you sign up and nothing is charged that day. We charge it for what your campaigns spent when your unpaid usage reaches a threshold (currently $50, then $200, then $500), or at the end of the month, whichever comes first. If a charge is declined, sending stops until it is paid. Post-paid is not available on every payment method (for example some prepaid cards, or cards issued in some countries): we may then ask you to use another card or to switch to prepaid credit. By saving a payment method you authorize these charges without further confirmation.
Card check. When you save a card, we may place a temporary authorization hold on it (for example $50) to check the card. A hold is not a charge. Your bank releases it after a few days, unless your campaigns reach that amount while the hold is active: we then use it toward your payment, only for what you owe, instead of a new charge. We may refuse a card that cannot take the hold.
Reserved follow-ups. When the first email of a sequence goes out, we reserve the cost of its follow-ups on your credit. Each follow-up is billed at its real cost when it is sent, and the reserve is released when it is not. Your dashboard shows billed spend and reserved amounts apart.

read_skill {"slug":"costs-roi-stats"} → {"slug":"costs-roi-stats","title":"Costs, ROI and stats","content":"# Costs, ROI and stats

Owners: runs-service (work done and its cost), features-service (usage, return), sales-lead-service (replies).

## Read (all free)
- get_spend_by_campaign(brandId, window) → GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId. list_recent_runs(brandId) → GET /v1/runs?brandId=.
- get_org_usage → GET /v1/features/orgs/usage: everything billed, by kind of work.
- get_offer_performance(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/revenue?brandId=: spend, emails, replies, return.
- list_sales_paths → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-paths: return per path. get_offer_sourcing → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing: return per source.
- list_replies_to_handle(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/leads?brandId=&offerId=&bucket=positive_reply: people who replied with interest and wait for the user.
- get_campaign_next_steps(brandId, campaignId) → GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns/{campaignId}/next-steps: what comes next in one campaign. Leads waiting for a send on any channel (nextSends.leadsQueued: follow-ups scheduled on email, WhatsApp... plus the email sender's queue), when the next send happens (nextSends.nextSendAt, in each lead's own working hours; scheduledFollowups.byDay per day), and the measured median days from a first email to a first positive reply (timeToFirstPositiveReply).

## "How are my campaigns doing?"
Tell it as a short story, one running campaign at a time (list_campaigns → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns, then get_campaign_next_steps for each):
1. It runs, its cap, what it used this period (list_campaigns: budget, maxBudget).
2. What waits and when it leaves: "47 leads are queued, the next go out Monday morning in their own working hours." Read nextSends only: leadsQueued (every channel), nextSendAt (the earliest moment, never an exact promise), dueNow (already due: they go at the next pass). leadsQueued null = say you cannot see the queue right now, never "nothing queued".
3. When replies come: ALWAYS say it, never skip this line. Measured (timeToFirstPositiveReply has a figure): "Expect a reply about <that figure> after the first email", and whose figure it is (basis): this campaign, or our clients on the same channel. Not measured (learning: true, or no figure): "It is too early to say how long replies take on this campaign." No number, no guess, no word "learning".
4. A reactive campaign acts on its trigger (runsWhen): say what starts it. No tool serves its delay: state none.

## Rules
- Use served figures only. Never add, average or estimate a figure yourself.
- Two figures disagree: file it for the team (request_staff → POST /v1/staff-requests, kind bug), silently; tell the client only what is certain (`client-comms`).

read_skill {"slug":"budget-and-billing"} → {"slug":"budget-and-billing","title":"Budget and billing","content":"# Budget and billing

Owner: billing-service. Amounts are in cents where the field says so.

## Read
- get_billing_account → GET /v1/billing/accounts: balance, credits, usage, payment mode (`payment_mode`).
- get_daily_budget(brandId) → GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/daily-budget, get_brand_pause(brandId) → GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/pause.
- Each campaign's budget: list_campaigns → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (its funnel caps, in words). Never the old per-step ceilings.

## Write
- set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one campaign's max budget and/or max volume (starts nothing).
- set_daily_budget(brandId) → PATCH /v1/brands/{brandId}/daily-budget: the brand's daily ceiling (0 pauses spend). Confirm the amount first.
- set_brand_pause → PATCH /v1/brands/{brandId}/pause: pause or resume the whole brand. Resuming starts spend again: get a yes first.

## Postpaid accounts (`payment_mode: postpaid`): billing is a non-topic
- It works like Google Ads: the card on file is charged automatically for what was spent. The person has nothing to pay, add or watch.
- Never mention a credit line, a charge threshold, adding funds, a top-up, paying now, a balance running out, a free credit to unlock, or billing holding or blocking a campaign. None of it applies. The only money the person decides is each campaign's budget.
- Only if the person asks how they are charged: "Your card is charged automatically for what you spend, like Google Ads." Nothing more.

## Prepaid accounts (`payment_mode: prepaid`)
- First payment or adding money: in the chat, after the person's yes on the amounts, create_prepaid_checkout gives a card payment link only they pay (get_prepaid_status first: active = already paid). On the web, the billing page (open_page) works too. An API agent prepays with POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout (MCP: distribute_prepay).

## Rules
- Every switch-on has at least one cap the user stated (budget and/or volume). Never propose one without it.","subSkills":[]}

Tes 3 campagnes tournent toutes sur la même offre, et voilà ce que chacune fait :

**1. Celle qui trouve de nouveaux prospects** (email à froid)
Elle sort de nouvelles entreprises (filtres, signaux d'achat, engagement LinkedIn) et leur envoie un premier email. Max $10/jour, et $10.06 déjà dépensés aujourd'hui : la limite est atteinte, donc plus de nouveau premier contact avant demain.

**2. Celle qui booke les rendez-vous**
Dès qu'une personne répond positivement, l'IA lui propose un créneau dans la minute, sans que tu aies à répondre. Jusqu'à $1/jour.

**3. Celle qui appelle**
Dès qu'une personne répond positivement, l'IA l'appelle pour fixer un appel. Elle n'a pas encore de plafond quotidien.

Depuis le début : 204 prospects contactés, 182 emails partis, 2 rebonds, 1 clic, et aucune réponse pour l'instant, pour $63 dépensés. C'est encore tôt pour dire en combien de jours arrivent les premières réponses, et rien n'attend de toi côté conversations aujourd'hui.

Le prochain pas utile : décider si on augmente le budget quotidien de la campagne email pour toucher plus de prospects, ou si on la laisse tourner encore quelques jours. Tu peux le faire dans l'onglet Campagnes ouvert à droite, ou me dire le montant et je l'applique.

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.
